evidenceExcerpts.exactLines:
5: ## Ordinary compelled Attack Actions
6: 
7: When an actual compulsion orders an ordinary Attack Action, use the target's native ordinary attack sequence, including inherent Extra Attack and an NPC's native Multiattack if that is actually its ordinary Action. No additional Action/attack is granted. A source expressly limited to one attack retains that limit: Confusing Flash is such an exception. An ordinary attack instruction is not permission to invent an Attack Action or convert another source's single attack into Multiattack.
8: 
9: Spend required ordinary ammunition normally. The command cannot activate consumable magic, special ammunition with a distinct expendable feature, RP/spellcasting, charges, recharge/per-rest abilities or optional finite-resource riders. Actual optional expenditures remain optional and cannot be compelled indirectly by choosing a method which requires them. Where instruction wording leaves the choice open, the target/controller may use a different legal ordinary method. If none satisfies the instruction, that instruction fails without spending a prohibited resource or manufacturing one. Existing source-specific limits and actual absolute prohibitions remain.

170: 
171: **Stacking:** A creature may be Charmed by more than one source; each source relation is tracked independently. Advantage does not stack.
172: 
173: **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Charm immunity prevents application. Forced actions from another effect are not made voluntary merely because the creature is Charmed.
174: 
175: **Compatible V6/source details:**

52: A living character at zero HP is Unconscious. Core's condition already includes Incapacitated, unawareness, dropping held items and falling Prone; an adjacent hit is critical as specified there. Healing does not silently remove other independent causes of Unconscious or Prone.
53: 
54: While dying, make one death save at the **start of each regular initiative turn**. Roll d20 without modifiers unless a feature specifically modifies death saves. Natural 20 restores 1 HP; natural 1 adds two failures. Other results of 10 or more add one success; 9 or less add one failure. Three successes make the creature Stable; three failures make it Dead. Extra turns and Actions add no extra death saves. Stable or Dead creatures do not roll them.
55: 
56: Regaining positive HP or becoming Stable resets both counters. Temporary HP does not raise normal HP, end Unconscious or reset counters. Fully absorbed damage does not end Stable or add a death failure in this provisional interpretation. Independent Maiming can still cause its Wound save.
57: 
58: **Stabilize:** an Action and DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check, or an Action using one healer's-kit use automatically, stabilizes a living dying creature at zero. It remains Unconscious and makes no death saves. Roll 1d4 once when it becomes Stable and record its absolute recovery time that many hours later. If still Stable then, it regains 1 HP. Damage reaching normal HP cancels that deadline and resumes dying with the appropriate failures. Rest and Stable recovery use the same elapsed clock, so four hours of recovery inside an eight-hour Watch do not cost twelve hours. A later rest does not separately replay the Stable healing event.

58: 
59: 1. Expire start-ending effects and apply immediate state changes from those expirations.
60: 2. Refresh Reaction; tick regular-start recharge/non-action clocks.
61: 3. Resolve already-due absolute state recovery if now legal, including a previously blocked Stable recovery deadline.
62: 4. If still alive, dying and at 0 HP with death saves, make that turn's death save.
63: 5. Resolve other start effects and periodic events in application order.
64: 6. Begin voluntary turn decisions.
65: 
66: At **end**, resolve triggered effects, due damage, saves and maintenance before end-ending effects expire; then the slot finishes. No extra turn creates another regular marker. The caller must not reuse a resolved marker.
67: 
68: For simultaneous effects, earlier application timestamp precedes later. For simultaneous components of one source, its printed internal order controls; otherwise use stable application sequence, with source/mechanical ID as a final tie-break. Record that sequence when creating the effects. Beneficial/harmful labels do not change priority. Periodic family arbitration happens once per family/marker before its damage, retaining the family registry's consumed loser ticks.

1: # Decennium Descent — active development direction
2: 
3: Effective 16 October 2026, Decennium Descent is a **video game only**. Tabletop/TTRPG development is retired by the owner. The [verbatim directive](mechanics/VIDEO_GAME_ONLY_DIRECTIVE.md) takes precedence over conflicting tabletop requirements in older plans and the [original accelerated review protocol](mechanics/SPELL_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md). evidenceExcerpts.exactText: Abjuration rank 3: a creature is opposed if at least one explicitly known axis is exact opposite to the snapshot (Lawful/Chaotic or Good/Evil). Neutral is never opposite; an unknown axis supplies no opposition, and does not erase a known opposite on the other axis. On an opposed creature's attempted entry from outside, roll its Wisdom save before entry, including forced movement, carriage or teleportation. REVIEWED CADENCE CLARIFICATION: record that success or failure for this source character, mode and target until the target's next regular-start marker; the current in-progress start never counts. A success permits entries during that window; failure blocks all non-Falling entry attempts during it without repeat rolls. Same-caster replacement/recasting does not reset this window. Outside initiative, use a fixed 6-second window and preserve its deadline if initiative starts. A failed physical entry stops before the boundary; a failed teleport leaves the creature at its origin without refunding committed teleport costs. Conjuration rank 6: only a creature with both explicit canonical axes exactly matching both snapshotted axes may enter from outside. Unknown is not matching. Nonmatching physical entry, forced movement and carriage stop before entry; a teleport attempt to place a nonmatching creature inside leaves it at origin after costs are committed.
